summary: This is a purely additive audit tool (new verify_7day_task_completion.py script, a generated JSON+MD report, and a documentation-only MASTER_INDEX.yaml registry entry) with no deletions and no touches to .github/workflows/** or any other sensitive path (migrations, schema, auth, permissions, .env), so tier1 classification is correct. The script is architecturally sound: all subprocess calls use list-form args (never shell=True or string interpolation), so task IDs, branch names, and titles pulled from AI-generated task.yaml files cannot cause command injection even though they are effectively untrusted input; PR state is correctly resolved live via a single cached `gh pr list --state all` call per repo rather than trusting task.yaml's self-reported status, with sensible fallbacks (pr_url.txt, log grep, headRefName match, then commit-ancestry grep, then checkpoint-terminal-state for investigation-only tasks). It also implements a real, generalized title-vs-actual-PR mismatch detector that catches genuine prior misreporting (two tasks that claimed completion via unrelated PRs while their named PR was still open), which is a meaningful correctness improvement over trusting self-reports. Minor non-blocking concerns: concurrent `git fetch` calls against shared local clones under /opt/veridian/repos could contend with other running workers on the same repo, and `by_headref.setdefault` in gh_pr_list could pick an arbitrary PR if multiple PRs share a head branch name -- neither is a security issue and both are edge cases in a read-only reporting tool, not something that mutates production state.
issues: Non-blocking: default `do_fetch=True` runs `git fetch origin <branch>` against shared local repo clones under /opt/veridian/repos, which could contend with other concurrently running workers on the same clone -- consider defaulting to --no-fetch in automated/concurrent contexts.

Non-blocking: gh_pr_list's by_headref dict uses setdefault, so if multiple PRs (e.g. closed-then-reopened) share the same headRefName, the tool may attribute the wrong PR -- the method/URL are still disclosed transparently in the evidence, so this is a low-severity accuracy edge case, not a hidden failure.
